words.gloss: embryo; descent, entry (avakrānti: the entry of the soul and development of the embryo); body-section (śārīra)

hindi: अब इसके बाद हम गर्भावक्रान्ति शारीर की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the Śārīra (the section on the body) called Garbhāvakrānti, the descent (entry) of the embryo.
notes: Stock opening formula (atha ataḥ ... vyākhyāsyāmaḥ). Printed -krāṃti- is anusvāra for n (orthography). 'Garbhāvakrānti' is the title of the chapter; 'descent/entry of the embryo' is the literal sense.

words.gloss: in the receptacle (āśaya: womb, garbhāśaya; standard)
by ārtava (menstrual fluid, the female reproductive fluid; standard)
unclear: probably 'immediately, at once' (anu-akṣa); sense uncertain
passion; beginning with; afflictions (kleśa); sway, control; following

hindi: जब पुराना रज चला जाता है और नया रज स्थित हो जाता है, गर्भ के आशय यानी गर्भाशय में और मार्ग में शुद्धता होती है, तब बीज के रूप वाला, विकार रहित शुक्र यानी पुरुष का वीर्य, विकार रहित वायु से प्रेरित, अन्य महाभूतों से अनुगत, आर्तव यानी स्त्री के रज से मिला हुआ, सम्भवतः तुरन्त ही, राग आदि क्लेशों के वश में चलने वाले, अपने कर्म से प्रेरित, मन के समान वेग वाले जीव से संयुक्त होकर गर्भाशय में पहुँचता है।
english: When the old rajas (menstrual blood) has gone, the new one is established, and the receptacle of the embryo (the womb, garbhāśaya) and the passage are clean, the śukra (semen), in the form of seed, unaltered, impelled by unaltered wind (vāyu), followed by the other great elements (mahābhūta), mingled with ārtava (menstrual fluid), probably at once, and joined with the jīva (the living soul) that follows the sway of the afflictions beginning with passion, is impelled by its own action (karma) and is swift as the mind, goes to the womb.

text_flags.why: possible: the anusvāra before nu is not required (vaśa + anuvartin = vaśānuvartin)

notes: One long sentence, absolute locatives first (gate ... avasthite ... śuddhe), then the subject śukra with its qualifiers. 'anvakṣam' is not certain (taken as anu-akṣa 'at once'; the hedge 'probably' is in the translations); alternative senses not excluded. 'abhisaṃsṛṣṭaṃ' is read as agreeing with śukra. Reading: 'rajasinave' = rajasi + nave. 'sva-karma-coditena', 'manojavena' are qualifiers of jīva. Identification (modern equivalents): rajas = menstrual blood (standard, in this context; elsewhere also a guṇa); śukra = semen (standard); ārtava = menstrual fluid, the female reproductive fluid (standard); garbhāśaya = womb (standard); jīva = living soul (doctrinal, no modern equivalent).

hindi: कार्यों के कारण का अनुसरण करने के कारण वह उसी के स्वभाव को प्राप्त होता है।
english: And because effects follow their causes, it attains the nature of that (cause).

text_flags.why: possible: the print has a run of three t and lacks the 'a' of tat; the sense requires āt + tat-svabhāvatām

notes: The subject (the embryo, from unit 2) is not stated; 'it' is understood. Split follows the corrected reading; the printed form is kept in src.

words.gloss: napuṃsaka (a person neither male nor female)

hindi: और इसी कारण से शुक्र की अधिकता से पुरुष, आर्तव की अधिकता से स्त्री और उन दोनों की समता से नपुंसक।
english: And from that very cause: a male from the abundance of śukra (semen), a female from the abundance of ārtava (menstrual fluid), a napuṃsaka (neither male nor female) from the equality of the two.
notes: Elliptical: no verb is stated (a verb such as 'arises' is carried from the sense and is not supplied in the translation). The printed line runs words together (bāhulyātpumānārtavasyabāhulyātstrī); this is a spacing habit, not a typo. napuṃsaka is the third category (lit. 'not male'); no single modern equivalent is asserted.

words.gloss: śukra and ārtava (semen and menstrual fluid)

hindi: शुक्र और आर्तव के वायु से टुकड़ों में विभक्त हो जाने पर विभाग के अनुसार सन्तानों की उत्पत्ति होती है।
english: When śukra and ārtava (semen and menstrual fluid) are split into pieces by the wind (anila), there is the origin of offspring according to the divisions.
notes: Hindi 'होती है' renders the nominal sentence 'utpattiḥ' (copula understood). The text says 'offspring' in the plural; no count is stated or added. Token 4 fuses yathāvibhāgam + apatyānām + utpattiḥ (printed with no spaces).

hindi: विकृत होने पर अन्य योनि के आकार वालों की।
english: When vitiated: of those having the forms of other wombs.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue unit 5 (utpattiḥ, 'origin', is carried over), so the full sense would be 'when (they are) vitiated, the origin of those with forms of other wombs'; no verb or noun is supplied in the translation. 'viyoni' is read as 'other/different womb'; whether this means animal-like forms is not stated and is not added. What is vitiated (śukra and ārtava from 5, or the vāyu) is not stated.

words.gloss: just now; taken; whose foetus (she who has just conceived)

hindi: अब सद्यः गर्भ धारण की हुई स्त्री का लक्षण: योनि द्वारा बीज का ग्रहण, तृप्ति, भारीपन, फड़कना और शुक्र तथा आर्तव का अनुबन्ध।
english: Now the sign of a woman who has just conceived: the taking in of the seed by the yoni (vagina), satisfaction, heaviness, throbbing, and the continued connection of śukra and ārtava.

text_flags.why: spacing: two words run together (atha + nāryāḥ); certain

notes: 'nāryāḥ' read as gen. sg. of nārī 'woman'. 'yonyā' is read as instrumental ('by the yoni'); a genitive yonyāḥ 'of the yoni' is possible, and the sense changes little. 'gurimā' is nom. sg. of the masc. stem gurimān (usually garimān); it stands in a list of signs. 'sphuraṇam' read as a separate word (no sandhi needed after gurimā). Identification: yoni = vagina, female genital tract (standard).

words.gloss: by itself; being built up, increasing
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, pres. pass. part. upa-√ci, n. nom. sg.

hindi: तब वह नीचे रुका हुआ, अन्य, अन्य, अपने आप बढ़ता हुआ, अपरा यानी सम्भवतः आँवल, ऐसा कहते हैं।
english: Then that, checked below—other, other—increasing of itself, they call aparā (probably the afterbirth, placenta).

text_flags.why: possible: 'aparam aparam' may be a repeated word; the duplicate is kept in the translation

notes: Difficult line; the grammar is not secure. 'tat' is taken as the blood/fluid of the previous units (not stated here). The doubled 'aparam' could be a dittography, or mean 'one other thing, another thing'. 'aparā' (f.) is the standard Āyurvedic term for the afterbirth (placenta); the identification is probable, and the translation keeps the Sanskrit word. The reading 'aparā iti' is taken from 'aparetyāhuḥ'. Subject of 'āhuḥ' is unstated ('they').

hindi: जरायु यानी सम्भवतः गर्भ की झिल्ली, ऐसा दूसरे कहते हैं।
english: Others say: jarāyu (the foetal membrane).

text_flags.why: certain: a doubled u in the print; jarāyuḥ + iti gives jarāyur iti

notes: The verb 'say' is carried from unit 12 (āhuḥ) and appears in the translation as 'say' for the plural subject 'others'. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 12 (an alternative name for the same thing). jarāyu = foetal membrane / afterbirth (probable; the term is also used for membranes enclosing the foetus).

hindi: रक्त के स्थिर हो जाने पर रोमराजी यानी रोमों की पंक्ति प्रकट होती है, और रक्त ऊपर जरायु के शेष को प्राप्त होता है।
english: But when the blood has settled, a line of hair (romarājī) appears, and the blood goes upward to the remainder of the jarāyu.

text_flags.why: spacing: two words run together; certain

notes: Ambiguous: 'jarāyuśeṣam ... asṛk pratipadyate' could also mean 'the remainder of the jarāyu goes up as blood'. The first reading (asṛk subject, jarāyuśeṣam object) is taken. 'romarājī' is a line of hair; whose body it appears on is not stated. 'asṛk' (asṛj) is a synonym of rakta, both 'blood'.

words.gloss: plump; cheek; breast; state of being
black; lip; nipple; state of being

hindi: उससे मोटे गाल और स्तन होना तथा काले ओंठ और चूचुक होना।
english: From that, plumpness of cheeks and breasts, and blackness of lips and nipples.
notes: Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied. The tokens are printed joined (tasmātpīnakapolapayodharatākṛṣṇauṣṭhacūcukatvaṃ). payodhara (lit. 'milk-bearer') = breast; kapola = cheek; cūcuka = nipple (standard). Whose face and breasts is not stated; the sense is the signs of changes of pregnancy.

words.gloss: of her who has given birth

hindi: स्तनों में ही स्थित, अनुमानित पाठ पर कफ से रंजित, प्रसूता में स्तन्य यानी दूध की अवस्था को प्राप्त, फिर आहार के रस से पुष्ट होता है।
english: That which has its resting place in the breasts, on a conjectural reading tinged by Kapha, having reached the state of breast-milk (stanyatā) in her who has given birth, is nourished again by the rasa of food.

text_flags.why: possible: 'keṃpha' for kapha and an extra 'ta' in 'upataraṃjitaṃ'; the intended word is probably kapha-uparañjita 'tinged with Kapha'; reading uncertain

notes: Subject not stated (probably the blood of unit 14; not asserted). The reading 'tinged with Kapha' is conjectural (damaged-looking word keṃphopataraṃjitaṃ). 'rasa' here = nutrient fluid of food. Identification: stanya = breast milk (standard).

words.gloss: kalala (the first embryonic mass; early embryo, probable)

hindi: उनमें पहले मास में कलल यानी सम्भवतः आरम्भिक भ्रूण उत्पन्न होता है।
english: Of these, in the first month a kalala (the first embryonic mass, probably the early embryo) arises.
notes: kalala is the first stage of the embryo; the modern equivalent (zygote or early embryo) is probable, not exact.

hindi: दूसरे मास में घन, पेशी या अर्बुद, और उनसे क्रम से पुरुष, स्त्री और नपुंसक।
english: In the second month, a dense mass (ghana), or a peśī (muscle-like lump), or an arbuda (lump); from these, in order, males, females and neuters (napuṃsaka).
notes: No verb is stated or supplied. The pairing of ghana, peśī, arbuda with male, female, neuter is left to the order word 'kramāt' ('in order'); the text does not state the pairing and it is not stated as fact here. 'peśyarbudaṃ' = peśī + arbudam.

hindi: तीसरे मास में वह पाँच प्रकार से अंकुरित होता है।
english: In the third month it sprouts in five ways.
notes: Subject 'it' (the embryo) is understood.

hindi: वह जैसे कि।
english: Namely:
notes: Stock formula 'tad yathā', 'namely', introducing the list in unit 21.

hindi: दोनों सक्थि यानी जंघाएँ, दोनों बाहु और सिर।
english: The two thighs (legs), the two arms and the head.
notes: The list of the five sprouts of unit 19 (two legs, two arms, head = five). No verb. sakthi = thigh, also used for the leg.

words.gloss: thigh; beginning with; sprouting; one; time (at the same time as the sprouting of the legs and the rest)
birth; after; time; born (born after birth)

hindi: और पैरों आदि के अंकुरित होने के समय ही सब अंग, अवयव और इन्द्रियाँ एक साथ उत्पन्न होते हैं, केवल जन्म के बाद के समय में उत्पन्न होने वाले दाँत आदि को छोड़कर; किन्तु क्रम से वे स्पष्ट हो जाते हैं।
english: And at the very time of the sprouting of the thighs and the rest, all the limbs, parts and sense organs (indriya) come to be simultaneously, except those born in the time after birth, the teeth and the rest; but in order they become distinct.
notes: 'krameṇa tu spaṣṭībhavanti': the subject 'they' could be all the parts or only the later-born ones; the translation leaves it open. 'sakthyādi' = sakthi + ādi, 'the thighs and the rest' (the five sprouts of 21). 'indriya' = sense organ (standard); kept as indriya. 'sarvāṃgāvayaveṃdriyāṇi' is read as a series of three terms, not a closed compound.

hindi: यह प्रकृति है।
english: This is the prakṛti (the natural, normal state).
notes: Copula understood. Here prakṛti means the normal course (as against vikṛti in 24), not the body-type or the primal matter.

hindi: इससे अन्यथा विकृति है।
english: Otherwise than this is vikṛti (deviation, the abnormal state).
notes: Copula understood. Printed 'vikṛtirato'nyathā' = vikṛtiḥ + ataḥ + anyathā.

words.gloss: male; female; neuter; any one of; sign; conforming to

hindi: और गर्भ के, अपने अपने अनुसार, पुरुष, स्त्री या नपुंसक में से किसी एक के लिंग के अनुरूप ही भाव मन में और शरीर में स्थित होते हैं।
english: And, each according to its own, the states (bhāva) of the embryo that conform exactly to the sign (liṅga) of one of male, female or neuter become established in the mind and in the body.

text_flags.why: possible: 'anyatarma' appears to be anyatama (any one of several) with ra/ma confusion; the visarga after anurūpā is also missing before 'eva' (sandhi ā eva is normal)
possible: visarga normally stays before m of manasi; the print has bhāvā

notes: The reading of 'anyatarma' is uncertain: anyatara 'either of two' or anyatama 'any of many'; for three genders anyatama is expected. 'bhāva' translated 'state'; the text does not specify which states.

hindi: किन्तु लिंगों के मिश्रण में विशेष निर्धारण वहाँ से होता है जहाँ अधिकता हो; उससे भाव दोनों में से किसी एक के होते हैं।
english: But in a mixture of signs, the distinguishing (determination) is from where there is greater abundance; from that, the states are those of one or the other.

text_flags.why: possible: yava (barley) makes no sense here; 'yato ... tato' is the correlative pair
possible: plural nominative agreeing with bhāvāḥ

notes: Reading uncertain. 'vaiśeṣikaṃ' with spurious anusvāra is taken as the neuter nominative 'distinguishing (determination)'; the other reading, vaiśeṣika as a first member, is possible. The meaning of 'anyatarāḥ' ('of one or the other') is the best fit. Hindi 'होता है' renders a nominal sentence.

hindi: वह जैसे कि।
english: Namely:
notes: Stock formula 'tad yathā', introducing the list in unit 28.

hindi: नपुंसकता, भीरुता, आत्मविश्वास की कमी, मोह, अस्थिरता, नीचे भारीपन, कसाव की कमी, शिथिलता, मृदुता, गर्भाशय और बीज के भाव, तथा उसी प्रकार अन्य उचित भी, ये स्त्री बनाने वाले भाव हैं।
english: Klaibya (unmanliness), timidity, lack of confidence, bewilderment, unsteadiness, heaviness below, lack of compactness, laxity, softness, the states of the womb and seed, and likewise other fitting (ones): these are the woman-making states.
notes: The list in 28 and the closing 'strīkarā bhāvāḥ' are one sentence: the listed states are 'woman-making states'. 'garbhāśaya-bīja-bhāvāḥ' is taken as 'states of womb and seed' (as in the womb and seed of a woman); the exact sense of the first-member relation is not secure. 'yuktāḥ ... apare' is read 'and other fitting (ones)'; 'yukta' may also mean 'joined, connected'. The print 'strīkarābhāvāḥ' = strīkarāḥ bhāvāḥ. klaibya is not simply impotence; here a character-trait of unmanliness; modern equivalent (impotence/lack of virility) is probable.

hindi: इनसे विपरीत पुरुष बनाने वाले हैं।
english: Those opposite to these are the man-making (ones).
notes: 'bhāvāḥ' is understood from 28. The sentence is nominal: copula understood.

hindi: मिले जुले नपुंसक बनाने वाले हैं।
english: The mixed (ones) are the neuter-making (ones).
notes: 'bhāvāḥ' understood from 28; copula understood.

hindi: और तब इसकी चेतना पूर्ण रूप से प्रकट हो जाती है।
english: And then its consciousness (cetanā) becomes fully manifest.

text_flags.why: spacing: words run together (ca + asya + cetanā); certain

notes: 'asya' refers to the embryo.

hindi: और तब से वह हिलता है और पाँचों इन्द्रियों के विषयों में अभिलाषा करता है।
english: And from then on it moves (throbs) and has desire for the five objects of the senses.

text_flags.why: likely: 'iṃdviya' is a letter scramble of indriya (dvi/dri)

notes: 'abhilāṣaṃ karoti' literally 'makes desire'. Subject 'it' (the embryo) understood. 'spandate' may mean 'moves' or 'throbs'.

hindi: क्योंकि इसका हृदय माता से उत्पन्न है और उसके रस को ले जाने वाली धमनियों यानी वाहिनियों द्वारा माता के हृदय से जुड़ा रहता है।
english: For its heart is born of the mother, and is joined to the mother's heart by dhamanīs (vessels) that carry its rasa.
notes: 'tad' in 'tadrasa' is not clearly stated: it may mean 'the rasa of that (mother)' or 'of that (the heart)'; 'its rasa' in the translation is a literal placeholder for that. dhamanī = vessel (tube-like channel); whether it means artery or umbilical vessel is not stated and is not asserted. The printed token runs words together (tadrasahāriṇībhirdhamanībhirmātṛhṛdayenābhisaṃbaddhaṃ). hṛdaya = heart (standard).

hindi: और इसी प्रकार दो हृदय वाली स्त्री को दौर्हृदिनी कहते हैं।
english: And so they call a woman with two hearts (dvihṛdayā) daurhṛdinī (a woman with longings).

text_flags.why: possible: hṛ printed as ha; daurhṛdinī from daurhṛda 'longing' is expected

notes: 'dvihṛdayā' = literally 'two-hearted'; used of a pregnant woman. 'daurhṛda' (longing of a pregnant woman) is the standard term. Whether the 'two hearts' refers to the mother's heart and the embryo's heart is not stated here.

hindi: दूसरे लोग तीन पक्ष से लेकर पाँचवें मास तक दौर्हृद का काल बताते हैं।
english: Others, however, give the time of the daurhṛda (longing) as from three fortnights up to the fifth month.

text_flags.why: possible: 'daurhada' for daurhṛda (hṛ printed as ha)

notes: 'ā pañcamāt māsāt' = up to the fifth month; whether the fifth month is included is not clear. Three fortnights is one and a half months.

hindi: और इच्छा तीव्र होने पर इसे कामनानुसार, अहित भी हो तो हित के साथ मिलाकर, देना चाहिए।
english: And when the wish is intense, one should give her, as desired, even the unwholesome, joined with the wholesome.
notes: 'hitopasaṃhitam' is read as 'joined with the wholesome'; the text does not say what is joined. No nouns are supplied (the objects are neuter adjectives). The subject of 'dadyāt' is unstated ('one').

words.gram: pres. part. anu-√car, m. nom. sg.

hindi: क्योंकि दौर्हृद की उपेक्षा से कुपित वायु शरीर के भीतर घूमती हुई गर्भ का नाश या विकृत रूप कर सकती है।
english: For, from disregard of the daurhṛda (longing), the wind (vāyu), agitated and moving about inside the body, may cause destruction or deformity of the embryo.

text_flags.why: likely: spurious ṃ before the avagraha

notes: 'vināśa' (destruction of the embryo) is the loss of the pregnancy, i.e. probably miscarriage; the translation keeps 'destruction'. 'vimāna' = disregard, dishonouring (of the wish). The print 'daurhṛdavimānāddhi' = daurhṛda-vimānāt + hi. 'kuryāt' read as optative 'may cause'.
